newsitem.title: USA: Clinton lauds Harriman as gifted public servant.
newsitem.headline: Clinton lauds Harriman as gifted public servant.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Wednesday eulogised U.S. Ambassador to France Pamela Harriman, shortly after her death in Paris, as "one of the most unusual and gifted people I ever met" and a great public servant.

"She was an extaordinary U.S. ambassador ... earning the trust of the leaders (of France) and the admiration of the people," Clinton said as he departed the White House for a trip to Georgia. "She was one of the most unusual and gifted people I ever met."

Harriman, a prominent Democratic party fund-raiser and Clinton supporter, died in a Paris hospital on Wednesday of a brain haemorrhage, aged 76. She had fallen ill on Monday evening during an excercize swim.

"Our country will miss her," Clinton said. "We are deeply indebted to the work she did in France in maintaining our relationships with one of our oldest and closest allies. She was a source of judgment and inspiration to me, a source of constant good humour and charm and real friendship and we will miss her very very much.

Clinton termed Harriman, a British-born naturalised American citizen, "another immigrant who became a great American." She was born in Farnborough, England, and became a U.S. citizen after marrying her third husband, the late multimillionaire diplomat Averell Harriman, in 1971. She was a daughter-in-law of the late British Prime Minister Winston Churchill by her first marriage.
Clinton said her body would be returned to the United States later this week and that funeral arrangements were pending.
